<!-- pr-reviewer: 642cd6947b557e43eb05c58d9cf6015d8be8e28e -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after #1020, which this PR is stacked on; only the second commit, 642cd694, was reviewed as this PR's own delta).

Reviewed at the high tier because it feeds the index-swing collision law.

**What looks good**
- Sign and units: the effective figure is `nose - s.thickness` (`posting_index_swing.rs`, the `Rise::Stack` arm). A raised centerline brings the spindle nose nearer, so subtracting is the right direction. Stack thickness, nose and messages are all mm. A stated figure replaces the nose as-is.
- No stale verdict: `index_swing_problems` (called from `posting.rs:662`) recomputes `rotary_stack::rise` from the world on every post. Nothing is cached, so a subplate resize, a plate re-thickness or a stated-figure edit shows at once.
- Unusable input is refused by name rather than judged on the table figure: a stack of unknown thickness (imported plate, vanished plate, loop, non-finite or non-positive figure), a stated figure that is no length, and an effective nose at or under zero. A setup without a subplate or a stated figure takes the `Rise::Table` path, so its message is unchanged. A pinning test covers this.
- Placement is undoable: `PlaceOnPlate`, `SetPlate` re-seat and `SetAccessory` resize all apply the pin law (`pins_fit`, 0.05 mm) at creation. The new `SetSetupNoseToAxis` validates at creation (finite, > 0, <= 5000 mm, no-op refused), and `invert` restores the previous value. `place_on_plate`, `add_accessory`/`set_accessory`, `get_rotary_stack` and `set_setup_nose_to_axis` cover MCP, and the UI queues the same command.
- Save/load is additive: the `nose_to_axis` key is `serde(default)`, and a non-finite value is filtered when written. Old files load unchanged (pinned).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/raw numeric casts added in non-test code. Layering is respected and the schema component is only in `schema.rs`. New modules carry provenance lines, the new files are under ~400 lines, and the decision file is `docs/decisions/821-rotary-on-plate-stack.md`. No snapshot PNG, CHANGELOG, `.claude/` or AGENTS.md change, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is needed. The body has `Changelog:` and `Refs #821` (explained: the hardware check stays with the user).

**Local results** (PR head trial-merged with current upstream/main, clean merge; own worktree and target)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| rotary_subplate | 7/7 |
| mcp_rotary_stack | 1/1 |
| index_swing_horizontal | 10/10 |
| index_swing | 9/9 |
| builtin_accessory | 3/3 |
| rotary_fixtures | 4/4 |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 12/12 |
| fixture_plate / _riders / _followups | 7 / 7 / 4, all ok |
| mcp_plate, mcp_accessory | 1/1 each |
| fixtures, setups, setup_post_options, accessory_collisions | 14, 12, 10, 2, all ok |
| ui lib filters `setup_rotary accessory fixture structural` | 51/51 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The UI part (the Machine page "Rotary centerline" section and the "Rotary subplate" dialog entry) is covered by AccessKit label tests only. It needs the maintainer's hand check.
2. The stack is subtracted from every judged work-turning rotary in the setup, including a machine-built trunnion that is not under the subplate. That errs on the conservative side (more refusals), but a stated figure is the way out. Worth a line in the docs.
3. The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table does not list the new tools, as the body says. A follow-up is fine and then needs a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
